title: Juicy Slow-Cooked Southern-Thai Pork Tenderloin Bowl
description: A light and tangy Southern-Thai inspired dish featuring slow-cooked pork tenderloin with a hint of lemongrass and galangal, served in a crispy rice bowl with fresh herbs and pickled carrots.

ingredients.name: Shio-koji cure
ingredients.notes: available at most Asian grocery stores or online

instructions: Preheat a kazan or large Dutch oven to 300°F (150°C).
Mix the shio-koji cure, fish sauce, brown sugar, and rice vinegar in a small bowl to make the marinade.
Coat the pork tenderloin with the rice flour, shaking off any excess.
Slow cook the pork in the preheated kazan for 3 hours, or until tender and juicy.
Meanwhile, peel and slice the lemongrass and galangal, and add to the kazan for the last 30 minutes of cooking.
In a separate pot, heat some oil over medium heat and fry an egg until cooked through.
Cook the rice according to package instructions and let cool.
Pickled carrots can be made by slicing carrots thinly and soaking in a mixture of rice vinegar and sugar for at least 30 minutes.
To assemble the bowls, place a scoop of cooked rice in the bottom, followed by a slice of pork, a fried egg, and a handful of pickled carrots.
Garnish with fresh herbs like cilantro or scallions, and serve immediately.
